title_prefix: Connecting a block leaves the confirmed
mechanism: Core's BlockConnected (refs/bitcoin/src/node/txdownloadman_impl.cpp:98-110) does three things per block transaction: insert txid and wtxid into the recently-confirmed filter AND call m_txrequest.ForgetTxHash on both ids, dropping every peer's tracked announcement of a transaction the block just confirmed. It then keeps a second guard: GetRequestsToSend (:264-285) re-runs AlreadyHaveTx on every requestable announcement immediately before turning it into a getdata, and ForgetTxHash's anything that now passes, described in-tree as 'just a belt-and-suspenders'. Ours does only the first third. note-block-connected (src/validation/block.lisp:2624-2648) fills *recent-confirmed-txs*, rebuilds *most-recent-block-txs* and clears the compact-block cache, and never touches the tracker; grep over src/ shows the tracker is cleared only at tx receipt (protocol.lisp:1847-1849), notfound (:484), peer disconnect (:499), request timeout (:603) and node start (src/node/init.lisp:1313) -- nothing on block connection. The scheduler cannot compensate: process-tx-requests (src/networking/protocol.lisp:530-562) and retry-timed-out-tx-requests take no arguments at all, so they have no mempool, no utxo set and no filter to re-check against. Our inv-time gate %already-have-tx-p (protocol.lisp:705-729) does match Core's AlreadyHaveTx, so a hash that is already confirmed when the inv arrives is never tracked; the exposure is the announcements already sitting in the tracker when the block connects, plus anything that enters the mempool by a non-P2P route (RPC submission, a 1p1c package member) between the inv and the getdata.
consequence: After every block we send getdata for transactions we already know are confirmed, and a Core peer answers them in full out of m_most_recent_block_txs, so we pay a whole redundant transaction download that handle-tx then discards on its recently-confirmed check (protocol.lisp:1858-1861). The waste is one transaction body per confirmed transaction that still had an outstanding tracker announcement at connection time, bounded above by the block's transaction count and in practice far smaller, since most block transactions were already downloaded into our mempool and had their announcements cleared at receipt. No transaction is lost and no peer gains a usable lever: an attacker cannot enlarge the set by announcing already-confirmed hashes, because %already-have-tx-p refuses to track them at inv time; it would have to keep announcements alive for transactions we do not yet have and then have a block confirm them. Bounded inefficiency, so S3.
evidence: Probe ga11-txrelay-block-connect (scripts/dev.sh load + eval), warm image bitcoin-lisp-sbcl:2.6.5-4. (1) Positive control that the scheduler is live and the count is real: (:SENT-WITH-EMPTY-TRACKER 0 :SENT-WITH-ONE-READY 1). (2) The finding, note-block-connected on a two-transaction block containing the announced transaction, candidate ready time backdated: (:RECENTLY-CONFIRMED T :TRACKER-ENTRY-SURVIVED T :GETDATAS-SENT-FOR-A-CONFIRMED-TX 1 :SERVABLE-FROM-MOST-RECENT-BLOCK T) -- we know it is confirmed, the announcement survives, the scheduler still requests it, and it is servable from the most-recent-block map, which is what a Core peer answers from. (3) The scheduler's structural inability to re-check: (:SCHEDULER-ARGLIST NIL :GETDATAS-SENT 1) -- process-tx-requests has an empty lambda list. Ours: src/validation/block.lisp:2624-2648; src/networking/protocol.lisp:530-562, :566-637, :705-729, :1847-1861; src/node/init.lisp:1313. Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/node/txdownloadman_impl.cpp:98-110, :125-148, :264-285.
fix_shape: Port both halves of Core's guard. First, drive ForgetTxHash from block connection: note-block-connected already walks every transaction in the block, so add a call that clears the tracker for the txid and the distinct wtxid of each one, mirroring txdownloadman_impl.cpp:107-108. The layering obstacle is that the tracker lives in bl.net, which loads after bl.val, so the call cannot be written directly -- route it through the existing bl.vi validation-hook seam the way the other upward references were converted, registering the networking clear function as a block-connected hook at node start rather than making validation depend on networking. Second, add the belt-and-suspenders re-check: give process-tx-requests and retry-timed-out-tx-requests the mempool and rejects filter (or a closure supplied at node start) so each requestable hash passes through %already-have-tx-p with include-reconsiderable false immediately before the getdata is built, and on a hit call tx-request-received for that hash instead of requesting it, exactly as GetRequestsToSend does at txdownloadman_impl.cpp:280-283. The second half alone would close the observable cost, but Core keeps both and the first is what stops the tracker carrying dead entries at all.
